title: 4-D photoacoustic tomography: the exploration of space and time in living tissue
protocol: Switch on the laser and let it warm up for ~15 min to stabilize its output.
Seal the window at the bottom of the water container with new polyethylene membrane.
Fill the water container with deionized water, which acts as an ultrasonic coupling medium between the ultrasonic detector and the sample.
Connect the transducer array, amplifier box, A/D cards, computer, and power supplies.
Inject 1 mg kg\(^{-1}\) of Urethane intra-peritoneally into the rat.
Wait until the animal is fully anesthetized.
Remove hair from the brain and surrounding area using hair removal cream.
Protect the eyes of the mouse with ointment.
Plant a venous catheter into the tail vein of the mouse and retain it with fixation tape.
Fill the catheter with 0.9% (vol/vol) NaCl solution to prevent blood clotting.
Place the mouse into the animal holder, place its snout into the breathing mask and fix its position with fixation tape.
Apply a layer of ultrasound gel onto the depilated area.
Apply another layer of ultrasound gel at the bottom of the membrane to seal the window of the water container.
Avoid trapping air bubbles inside the ultrasound gel; use a swab to squeeze out any trapped bubbles from the imaging area.
Insert the animal holder into the imaging chamber with linear stage.
Adjust the height of the animal holder to keep the animal head in the center of the ultrasound transducer array.
Start the data acquisition program and select the correct acquisition parameters.
Record data length: for example, 1000 points with 50 MHz sample rate for the record length are sufficient to fit a FOV of 30 mm.
Input the correct gain range from 0 to 80 dB.
Adjust the input-signal ranges of all channels to fully use the dynamic range of the data acquisition card.
Choose the number for signal averaging to balance between SNR and acquisition time.
Adjust the channel filtering according to the center frequency and bandwidth of the ultrasonic detector.
Choose an appropriate wavelength set for the imaging contrast agent.
Start the laser firing. Wear laser safety glasses when laser is on.
Execute the imaging loop shown in Figure 3a.
Stop the laser when acquisition is completed.
Inject contrast medium via catheter into the tail vein of the animal.
Repeat steps 13-15 when contrast agent is ready to be monitored.
Lower down the animal holder.
Stop the breathing anesthesia system.
Release the animal.
Clean the ultrasound gel off the animal body.
If future experiments on the same animal are necessary, house the animal according to the approved animal protocols.
Otherwise, euthanize and dispose of the animal by following proper procedures.
Reconstruct photoacoustic images using MATLAB based code.
Choose appropriate filters for pre-processing of raw data.
Remove low-frequency bias and high-frequency noise.
Normalize each reconstruction with the corresponding laser energy.
Use Amira for 3D reconstruction of photoacoustic image slices.
Make 4-D movies by MATLAB based code.
